chapter: Army band, Lena Horne, Billie Holiday and the 1950s
title: Billie Holiday's habits on the road and John Levy's provoking
summary: On dates in Boston and Detroit Billie wandered off with her chihuahua to bars between shows, and her husband John Levy deliberately made her angry before she went on, after which she sang with tears.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Billie Holiday as the musicians knew her

blocks.x: Right. We had to play up in New England, up in Boston, around that vicinity. She had some one

there -- then we jumped from there to Detroit, Michigan in a beautiful nightclub. And She was quite a girl, and the only thing about it, she had no conception of the time of day. Like in her contract, if she had four shows after she did her first show, she would take her little dog, her little chihuahua, which was given to her by Xavier Cugat, by the way. She'd take her little dog for a walk, and she'd walk up the street, and the first convenient bar that was open that she passed, she'd go in and sit at the bar, and she'd just sit up there and be friendly with people, and she would forget that in another hour or 45 minutes, she had another show to do. And if you didn't stay with her, she was there. And so, you just had to stay with her, you know, but she was so friendly and nice, and once she got on stage, Lady Day did her thing.

And I remember once in Boston, Massachusetts, her husband always tried to work a psychological on her, which I never approved of, but I couldn't do anything about it. He always made it a habit of making her mad five minutes before she got ready to go on stage to perform. He would walk in and peep in the door and call her a name or something, and she'd take her shoe off and throw it at him and start swearing, and start crying. And at the same time, she's putting her evening gown on, but she would go out on that stage with tears in her eyes, and give one of the greatest performances that Billie Holiday has ever given, you know. And mad with John Levy, her husband. But (inaudible) nobody knew it.
I just thought this -- it happened once, you know. But I found out it was a regular thing.
